title: How to choose an SEO agency in Singapore or Malaysia
excerpt: How to evaluate SEO agencies in Singapore and Malaysia: audits, reporting, red flags and the questions to ask. Find out more.
rm_title: SEO agency: how to choose one in SG & MY
rm_desc: How to choose an SEO agency in Singapore or Malaysia: the audit to demand, the reporting to inspect, red flags and the questions to ask. Read the checklist.
content: Search for "seo agency" in Singapore or Malaysia and you will get lists: ranked, sponsored and mostly interchangeable. Lists do not tell you how an agency behaves in month three. These criteria do. We are an agency ourselves, so read this knowing where we stand; every test here is one we are prepared to be measured against.
Demand a real audit before you sign

Any SEO agency worth engaging can show you specific problems on your actual site before a contract exists: crawl issues, structural problems and content gaps, with evidence. Be fair about depth: a pre-contract review is hours of work at most, so expect a sharp diagnosis of a few real issues; the full version is rightly part of the engagement. A generic PDF with your logo on it is a mail merge. The audit is also your preview of how they think and communicate, which is most of what you are buying.

Ranking reports alone are theatre. Ask to see a real (anonymised) client report: does it connect organic performance to leads, revenue, or pipeline? Does it cover search alongside the other channels you run, so budget decisions get made across them? An SEO agency that cannot show attribution beyond positions is optimising for its own renewal.
Ask who at the SEO agency does the work

The people in the pitch and the people in your account are frequently different people. Ask directly: who runs this engagement, what is their seniority, and how many accounts do they carry? Thin answers here explain most agency disappointments in this region.

Case studies should name outcomes. The kind of specificity to expect: organic sessions up 86% in a month after a technical rebuild; a target keyword from unranked to position 3; clicks up 34% in a first month with 2,553 keywords ranking; qualified leads up 150% after a restructure. Those are results from our own client work, and here is the nuance every case-studies page, ours included, owes you: the results on the page are the best ones on file. Ask any agency what a median engagement looks like, and what a failed one looked like and why. The answer to the second question tells you more than any case study. The point of the numbers is their shape, whoever you are evaluating: dated, measured, attributable. Google's own SEO starter guide is worth skimming first, so you can tell whether an agency's pitch matches what the platform itself says matters.
Red flags that end the meeting

Guaranteed rankings (nobody controls Google). Secret methods. Reporting only inside the agency's own tool. Refusal to itemise media or third-party costs. And be sceptical of both extremes on commitment: perpetual lock-ins are a trap, and "cancel anytime" is often a confession that nothing compounding is being built. We ask for a four-month minimum on SEO precisely because honest SEO needs that long to show its first real returns.
What happens after the contract is signed

The evaluation does not stop at the pitch. Ask for the first thirty days in writing: what gets audited first, when you will see the first report, and who signs off on the priority list. An SEO agency that cannot answer this before you have paid anything will improvise it after you have, and improvisation is expensive when it is billed monthly. The best proxy for how an engagement will run is how precisely the agency can describe the first month before it starts.
A simple scorecard for comparing each SEO agency

When you have two or three proposals side by side, memory and charm will decide for you unless you write the criteria down first. Score every SEO agency against the same short list, and weight the items by what matters to your business.
• Did they find real problems on your site before you signed?
• Is the first ninety days specific, with named deliverables and owners?
• Does the reporting tie organic work to leads or revenue?
• Do you know who does the work, and how many accounts they carry?
• Are the case studies dated, measured and honest about what was and was not typical?
• Is the contract clear on length, exit, ownership and costs?
A scorecard stops the loudest pitch from winning by default.
Talk to the agency's past clients

Any SEO agency can supply references, so ask for one that is similar to you in size and market, and one that has left. Ask what changed in the first six months, how the agency handled a bad month, and whether the reports were understandable. Ask what they would do differently. People are usually candid when the question is concrete, and the answers tell you more than the proposal does.
Keep ownership of your own accounts

Whatever the agency does, the assets should stay yours: the website and its hosting, the analytics property, Search Console, the Google Business Profile and any content produced for you. Insist on being the owner and giving the agency access. If a relationship ends, you should be able to walk away with your data and your history intact.

A strong in-house marketer can handle content and basic on-page work. Technical audits, large migrations and link-building usually need a depth of experience that one hire cannot cover. A common middle path is to keep day-to-day content in-house and use an SEO agency for strategy, technical work and measurement.

Whichever way you lean, give the first quarter a clear brief and a simple review date. A good SEO agency welcomes a written plan and a scheduled check-in, because it makes the work easier to defend. One that avoids both is telling you something about how the rest of the engagement will go.
Questions about choosing an SEO agency
How long before SEO shows results?
Expect a few months before movement is clear, and longer in competitive categories. Anyone promising a fixed date for first-page rankings is guessing, or selling something other than honest SEO.
Is a cheaper local agency fine?
It can be, if the scope fits and the work is real. The test is the same at any price: what is done each month, by whom, and how is it measured. Cheap is a risk only when it replaces those answers.
Then compare pricing knowing the market

Once an SEO agency clears these bars, price it against the market: we have published what SEO actually costs in Singapore and Malaysia. And if you would like to run these tests on us, start a conversation. The first one includes the audit.
